subtopics.title: Two Kinds of Scale and What They Promise

questions.question: On a plan drawn to 1 : 50, one centimetre on the page represents:
Why does a bar scale stay correct on a photocopied or resized plan when the ratio does not?
options: The bar scale is printed on the page, so it shrinks or stretches with the drawing
Bar scales are drawn oversized on purpose
The bar scale ignores units entirely

questions.question: On a touring map at 1 : 500 000, one centimetre represents:
Comparing 1 : 50 and 1 : 100 for the same page size:
options: 1 : 100 shows more detail because the number is bigger
1 : 50 shows more detail; the bigger the second number, the smaller the drawing relative to reality

subtopics.title: From Ruler to Reality — and Back

questions.question: A wall measures 9,0 cm on a 1 : 50 plan. Its real length is:
A 4,8 m stoep drawn at 1 : 100 appears on the page as a line of:
Carpet for a 4,50 m by 3,20 m room at R165,00 per m² costs:
A 9,6 m² stoep is paved with blocks 0,25 m by 0,20 m, plus 5% for breakage. Blocks needed:
A floor plan is a view:
options: From the front, standing in the garden
From an angle, showing two sides at once
From directly above, as though the roof were lifted away
Through a cut in the middle of the house

questions.question: The quarter-circle arc drawn across a gap in a wall shows:
options: The position of a ceiling light

questions.question: A dimension of 4 500 written on a builder's floor plan usually means:
Which answer about a layout would earn the most marks?
options: The plan shows a bedroom, a bathroom and a stoep
Hinge the door on the other side so it opens flat against the wall instead of into the passage
The plan has a north arrow

subtopics.title: Elevation Plans and What They Add

questions.question: An elevation plan shows:
options: Wall heights, the roof shape and how high the windows sit
The floor area of each room
How the rooms connect to one another
The thickness of the internal walls

questions.question: The 'north elevation' of a house is:
options: The northern half of the floor plan
The wall the north arrow is drawn on
The side of the house that faces north
The tallest wall of the house

questions.question: With a perimeter of 15,4 m from the plan and a height of 2,6 m from the elevation, the gross wall area is:
After deducting a door of 1,89 m² and a window of 1,5 m², the wall area to be plastered is:
To go from a measurement on the page to the real measurement, you:
A 6,4 cm line on a 1 : 50 plan represents a wall of:
Reading '1 : 100' as a shrinking factor means the drawing is:
options: One hundred times smaller than reality
One hundred times larger than reality

subtopics.title: The Bird's Eye and the Standing-in-Front View

questions.question: Which question can ONLY be answered by the elevation?
options: How big is the bedroom floor?
Does the door open into the passage?
Is the bathroom next to the bedroom?
How far above the floor does the window sill sit?

questions.question: On a floor plan, a thin triple line in a wall represents:
The elevation is described as which kind of view?
options: The standing-in-front view, looking straight at one wall
The bird's-eye view with the roof removed
A cut-away view through the roof

questions.question: Why does the north arrow on a floor plan matter to a family?
options: It marks the position of the front door
It fixes the scale of the drawing
It tells them which rooms will get sun and which face the weather
It shows which wall carries the plumbing

subtopics.title: Turning the Plan into a Shopping List

questions.question: Skirting for the 4,50 m by 3,20 m room, less a 0,9 m doorway, at R38,00/m costs:
Carpet uses area and skirting uses perimeter because:
options: Carpet covers the floor surface, while skirting runs around its edge
Skirting is cheaper per unit than carpet
Perimeter is easier to measure than area
Carpet is sold by the roll and skirting by the box

questions.question: Each paving block is 0,25 m by 0,20 m, so it covers:
The wall-area calculation needs both drawings because:
options: The two drawings use different scales
The plan gives the walk-around distance and the elevation gives the height
The elevation cannot be measured with a ruler
Complete questions always require two sources
